main_text.head: LOGICÆ VERÆ.
THESIS I.
main_text.p: DIalectica est ars bene differendi; id est, rationes rerum bene discernendi, & inter se componendi.
2. Rationes rerum vel simpliciter & seorsim considerantur, vel conjunctim & compositæ: Dialecticæ igitur duæ sunt partes, Inventio & Disposicio.
3. Inventio est prima pars hujus artis qua simplices rationes investigantur: singulæ enim inventionis regulæ sunt totidem viæ ac normæ rationes rerum discernendi.

4. Simplices istæ rationes dicuntur argumenta, quia affectum vel aptitudinem habent ad aliud aliquid arguendum: id est respectu, vel habitudine feruntur ad aliud aliquid: & eum à quo recte intelliguntur ad cogitationem illius secum ferunt.
5. Argumentorum alia in se vim habent arguendi, quia sunt in ipso artificio rei; atque adeo possunt ab artifice beneficio artis investigari; aliud vero non habet

page.notes: Text is in a roman type with long s rendered as s; the first word of Thesis I is a large initial D, read as "Dialectica". The last line is partly cut off at the right edge ("habet" completes the line as catchword and as a truncated line). Printed text at the right edge belongs to the facing page and has been left out apart from the note of its presence. Some words in the middle of the page are doubtful (e.g. "Disposicio", "seorsim") and may differ from the printed spelling; the printed text reads "Dispositio" and "fecum" in the original.
